primary_claim: Novel 'resample' control protocols, which dynamically re-sample suspicious agent actions, substantially outperform existing AI control protocols in a new multi-step BashBench agent environment, with the best protocol reducing a red-team attack success rate from 58% to 7% at only a 5% cost to a non-malicious agent's usefulness.

effect.metric: red-team attack success rate vs. usefulness cost on BashBench
effect.value: best protocol (resampling combined with analysis of previous steps) reduces attack success rate from 58% to 7% at a 5% cost to non-malicious-agent performance

stated_future_work: experiment with more powerful attacker models than GPT-4o mini in upcoming work
invest in studying more capable models now that multi-step control-eval techniques have been developed
discuss additional insights from the untrusted-monitoring game-tree analysis in a future post
optimize control protocols specifically based on their cost, an interesting direction for future research
test protocols in next-generation, more realistic control settings currently being built by several projects
limitations_stated: attacks were mostly constructed by human red-teamers rather than generated by the model itself, so the evaluation doesn't measure the model's own capability to produce such attacks
a weak untrusted model (GPT-4o mini) was used mainly for cost/latency reasons, limiting realism
resampling can be fairly expensive (up to 2x the calls to the untrusted model per task), with unclear real-world cost/latency implications
the BashBench tasks ended up more artificial and gamified than intended after filtering Stack-Overflow-derived scenarios for solvability
the red-team win condition (downloading and executing malware via pastebin) is narrow and doesn't generalize to arbitrary contexts
quote: our best protocol combines resampling with analysis of previous steps, reducing the success rate of attacks from 58% to 7% at a 5% cost to the performance of a non-malicious agent.
